column1: # CALL-GRAPH STRUCTURAL DIFFERENTIAL — CLOSED INVENTORY.
# WHY THIS EXISTS. GI-11's acceptance was an `observable`: a named Rust test that exists,
# is not ignored, and passes. Measured, an empty `#[test] fn …() {}` produces exactly
# `1 passed`, so the ENTIRE structural contract — scoped call-site identities, declared
# entry roots, an order-independent fixed point, per-edge completion, indirect targets
# resolved-or-declared — was satisfied by a body of `{}`. That is the sixth rung of the
# ladder this session has already climbed five times, and the boundary is known:
#     NO CHECK INSIDE THE ARTIFACT CAN ESTABLISH THAT A FUTURE REPLACEMENT IS GENUINE.
# The escape used for liveness works here too: pin OUTPUTS whose correct values are fixed
# by review, so what is checked is what the graph RETURNS, not that something ran. An
# empty test returns nothing and fails every row below.
# WHAT THIS FILE PINS, AND WHAT IT CANNOT. It pins the four contract clauses that are
# properties of a graph over a program, so a reviewer can fix their values by reading:
#   scoped call-site identities · declared entry roots · order-independent fixed point ·
#   per-edge completion · indirect targets resolved-or-declared.
# It CANNOT pin two others, because they are properties of the artifact and its test
# suite rather than of any program's graph:
#   * provenance tied to the compiled unit
#   * fault injection proving each verdict changes when its edge is removed
# Those are discharged by HUMAN REVIEW at the point GI-11 lands. The gate says so in its
# own output rather than implying this file covers them.
# COLUMNS (TAB-separated, all six mandatory):
#   id  property  source  expect  why  source-of-truth
# property: edges | roots | completion | indirect | identical-to
# expect:   the value the graph must return, normalized:
#   edges         caller>callee, comma-separated, sorted. Scoped where a bare name is
#                 ambiguous: `Buf::len` not `len`.
#   roots         comma-separated, sorted.
#   completion    caller>callee=yes|no, comma-separated, sorted. `no` means the edge may
#                 not complete — the callee can diverge.
#   indirect      resolved:<targets> or unresolved. SILENCE IS A FAILURE: a graph that
#                 simply omits an indirect call has not declared it.
#   identical-to  the id of another row whose graph this one's must equal exactly.
# id
scoped-identity
column5: two functions named `len` in different impls. A bare-name graph collapses them and reports an edge into Log::len that does not exist — the exact defect measured in src/effects/mod.rs:98

column1: entry-roots
column3: fn helper() -> i64 { return 1; }\nfn main() { helper(); }
column5: `main` is the only declared entry root; `helper` is reachable, not a root

column1: order-independent
column3: fn main() { helper(); }\nfn helper() -> i64 { return 1; }
column5: the same program with its definitions reordered must yield the same graph; a single forward pass over source order does not

column1: completion-diverges
column3: fn stop() { panic("x"); }\nfn after() -> i64 { return 1; }\nfn main() { stop(); after(); }
column5: the edge into `stop` may not complete, so the edge to `after` may not be taken either — per-edge completion is what makes this expressible

column1: indirect-declared
column3: fn target() -> i64 { return 1; }\nfn run(f: fn() -> i64) -> i64 { return f(); }\nfn main() { run(target); }
column5: the call `f()` has no statically visible target here. A graph may resolve it or declare it unresolved; omitting it silently is the failure this row exists to catch
